questions.text: Consider a graph [latex]G=(V,E)[/latex], where [latex]V=\{v_1,v_2,...,v_{100}\}[/latex], [latex]E=\{(v_i,v_j)|1\leq i \lt j\leq 100\}[/latex], and weight of the edge [latex](v_i,v_j)\; is \; |i-j|[/latex]. The weight of minimum spanning tree of G is _________
questions.solution:
Edge weight is |i [latex]-[/latex] j| [latex]\ge1[/latex], and weight 1 is possible only between consecutive vertices. The 99 edges [latex](v_i,v_{i+1})[/latex] form a spanning tree (a path) of weight 1 each.

Any spanning tree has 99 edges of weight at least 1, so this is minimum: 99.

Answer: 99

questions.text:
Let [latex]G=(V,E)[/latex] be a directed, weighed graph with weight function [latex]w:E\rightarrow \mathbb{R}[/latex]. For some function [latex]f:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R}[/latex], for each edge [latex](u,v) \in E[/latex], define [latex]w'(u,v)[/latex] as [latex]w(u,v)+f(u)-f(v)[/latex].

Which one of the options completes the following sentence so that it is TRUE?

"The shortest paths in G under [latex]w[/latex] are shortest paths under [latex]w'[/latex] too,_________".
questions.solution:
For any path [latex]s=v_0\rightarrow v_1\rightarrow\cdots\rightarrow v_k=t[/latex], the f-terms cancel in pairs:
[latex]w'(\text{path})=w(\text{path})+f(s)-f(t)[/latex]

Every s-to-t path changes by the same constant [latex]f(s)-f(t)[/latex], so the shortest one stays shortest, for any f. (This is the reweighting trick in Johnson's algorithm.)

Answer: for every [latex]f:V\rightarrow\mathbb{R}[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

if and only if [latex]\forall u \in V,f(u)[/latex] is negative
if and only if f(u) is the distance from s to u in the graph obtained by adding a new vertex s to G and edges of zero weight from s to every verex of G

questions.text: Let  [latex]G=(V,E)[/latex] be a weighted undirected graph and let T be a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of G maintained using adjacency lists. Suppose a new weighed edge [latex](u,v)\in V \times V[/latex] is added to G. The worst case time complexity of determining if T is still an MST of the resultant graph is
questions.solution:
Adding edge (u, v) creates exactly one cycle with T: the tree path from u to v plus the new edge.

T stays an MST unless the new edge is lighter than the heaviest edge on that path. Finding the path in a tree (DFS/BFS on T) and its heaviest edge takes [latex]\Theta(|V|)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(|V|)[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: For parameters a and b, both of which are [latex]\omega(1) , T(n)=T(n^{1/a})+1[/latex], and [latex]T(b)=1[/latex]. Then [latex]T(n)[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Each step takes the a-th root: [latex]n\rightarrow n^{1/a}\rightarrow n^{1/a^2}\rightarrow\cdots[/latex], until it reaches b.

[latex]n^{1/a^k}=b\Rightarrow\frac{\log_b n}{a^k}=1\Rightarrow k=\log_a\log_b n[/latex]

Each step adds 1, so [latex]T(n)=\Theta(\log_a\log_b n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(\log_a\log_b n)[/latex]
